nodes.title: Circle-equivariant p-typical cyclotomic spectra
nodes.statement: Write CycSp_T,p = LEq(id,(−)^{tC_p}:Sp^{BT} ⇒ Sp^{BT}), using T/C_p ≃ T by the p-th power map. An object is a T-spectrum X and a T-equivariant Frobenius X → X^{tC_p}; a morphism includes the homotopy intertwining Frobenius. This is Antieau–Nikolaus’s CycSp_p and AMMN’s CycSp. Distinguish it from the C_{p^∞}-equivariant category of RT.2/cyclotomic-spectrum. Restricting the action defines a functor to that category. Put TC_T,p(X)=map_CycSp_T,p(S^triv,X). Its equalizer is X^{hT} ⇉ (X^{tC_p})^{hT}; restriction compares it with TC(X|C_{p^∞},p) by a p-adic equivalence on bounded-below X. The underlying-spectrum functor is exact, conservative and colimit preserving.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Spectra, functor categories and all limits are coherent infinity-categorical objects.
proofSteps: Apply the existing lax-equalizer construction with the residual circle action; specify a single prime rather than forgetting the group acting on X.
Compute mapping spectra from the trivial cyclotomic sphere by the mapping-space formula. Compare the T and C_{p^∞} homotopy fixed-point equalizers after p-completion, keeping the comparison map.
acceptance: A consumer must specify whether its p-typical objects have T or C_{p^∞} actions; no uncompleted TC equivalence follows from restriction alone.

sources.match: The one-prime circle-action category and its TC conventions precede the cyclotomic t-structure.

nodes.title: Classical p-typical Cartier modules
nodes.statement: A p-typical Cartier module is an abelian group M with additive endomorphisms F,V satisfying F∘V=p·id_M. A morphism is an additive homomorphism commuting with both operators. Write Cart_p for this abelian category. Do not impose V∘F=p as a second axiom. Kernels and cokernels are those of abelian groups with their induced operators. A map f:M→N is an isogeny precisely when its underlying additive homomorphism is: if g:N→M satisfies gf=N₀id_M and fg=N₀id_N for N₀>0, then N₀g commutes with F,V and gives inverse composites N₀²id.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Spectra, functor categories and all limits are coherent infinity-categorical objects.
proofSteps: Define the operator structures and their commuting additive maps. Kernels and cokernels inherit FV=p; the forgetful functor creates these constructions.

The defects F_M g−g F_N and V_M g−g V_N land in ker f. Since N₀ kills ker f, N₀g commutes with both operators. This is the corrected lifting argument of AMMN, not the printed V/F mismatch (inherited RT.1 source issue E20).
acceptance: An additive approximate inverse need not commute with either operator until multiplied by its denominator.

sources.match: The classical operator relation and discrete realization underlie the cyclotomic heart.
Multiplying an additive approximate inverse removes its two operator defects.

nodes.title: Topological Cartier modules
nodes.statement: A p-typical topological Cartier module is a T-spectrum M with T-equivariant maps V:M_{hC_p}→M and F:M→M^{hC_p}, together with a specified homotopy F∘V ≃ Nm_{C_p}. The category TCart_p is the pullback of the coherent two-simplex category along (M,Nm_M), as in AN Definition 3.6; retaining the homotopy is part of the object and of its mapping spaces. A classical Cartier module gives HM with these maps via truncations. On π_iM, the induced F,V satisfy FV=p. The cofiber M/V=cofib(V) has cyclotomic Frobenius obtained from the square with V, F and the norm, followed by M^{tC_p}→(M/V)^{tC_p}. This defines a functor TCart_p→CycSp_T,p.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Spectra, functor categories and all limits are coherent infinity-categorical objects.
proofSteps: Use the arrow and two-simplex pullback of Definition 3.6, not an ordinary category of commuting maps. Proposition 3.8 computes its mapping spectra by a fiber sequence.
Take vertical cofibers of the square MhC_p→MhC_p over M→M^{hC_p}; the chosen norm-factorization homotopy induces M/V→M^{tC_p}. Compose with the Tate image of the quotient map.
For HM, the norm factors through multiplication by p on M, giving the classical case. The norm on general homotopy groups gives FV=p.
acceptance: The datum includes a norm-factorization homotopy and does not reduce to equalities on π_* alone.

sources.match: Topological Cartier data factor the norm coherently and the quotient carries a cyclotomic Frobenius.

nodes.title: Derived V-completeness
nodes.statement: A classical Cartier module M is derived V-complete when Rlim(…→^V M→^V M)=0 in D(ℤ), equivalently M≃Rlim_n cofib(V^n:M→M). A bounded-below topological Cartier module M is V-complete when lim_n M_{hC_{p^n}}=0 with the iterated V transition maps. Write V^n:M_{hC_{p^n}}→M for their composite and M/V^n for its cofiber. Its completion is lim_n M/V^n. For discrete HM the two completeness conditions agree. Ordinary separatedness or the ordinary inverse limit of cokernels is insufficient.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Spectra, functor categories and all limits are coherent infinity-categorical objects.
proofSteps: Define the two inverse towers, retaining derived limits and cofibers.

For discrete M compare the diagonal homotopy-orbit tower to the double tower with the classical V transition. AN Lemma 2.11 commutes uniformly bounded-below orbits and limits; the Milnor lim/lim¹ description supplies the converse.
The spectral completion universal property is supplied by tr-cartier-comparison, not assumed as part of the predicate.
acceptance: A completeness API must retain both lim and lim¹; naive V-adic completion loses the heart test.

sources.locator: Definition 3.20 and Proposition 3.22, p. 26; Definition 3.24 and Lemma 3.25, pp. 27–28
sources.match: These distinguish spectral V-completeness from the equivalent derived algebraic condition on discrete objects.

nodes.title: The cyclotomic t-structure
nodes.statement: CycSp_T,p has an accessible left-complete t-structure whose connective objects have connective underlying spectra. It is compatible with the symmetric monoidal structure. The underlying-spectrum functor is right t-exact and conservative, but is not left t-exact. Its connective part is the lax equalizer of id and τ_{≥0}(−)^{tC_p} on connective T-spectra. Write π_i^cyc for its homotopy objects. Products of connective objects are connective. No compatibility with filtered colimits of the heart is asserted. TCart_p has the t-structure whose connective and coconnective parts are detected on underlying spectra; TR and the heart comparison below relate the two.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Spectra, functor categories and all limits are coherent infinity-categorical objects.
proofSteps: Apply the presentable connective-subcategory criterion to the connective lax equalizer of AN Lemma 2.10; it is closed under extensions and colimits.

Use AN Lemma 2.11 to commute finite-group Tate with products of uniformly bounded-below T-spectra. The connective part is product closed; left separatedness follows from the conservative forgetful functor, so the imported completeness criterion proves left completeness.
The sphere unit and tensor products are connective. Define the TCart t-structure and its truncations using the norm factorization as in AN Definition 3.14 and Proposition 3.15, before applying TR.
acceptance: For a perfect characteristic-p ring k, THH(k) lies in the cyclotomic heart despite its positive even underlying homotopy. Consequently underlying spectral truncation cannot define cyclotomic truncation.
The heart is not closed under filtered colimits: the V=p, F=id Prüfer example has derived completion ℤ_p[1].

sources.locator: Theorem 2.1 and Lemma 2.10, pp. 8–10; Lemma 2.11, p. 10; Definition 3.14 and Proposition 3.15, pp. 22–23; Example 3.27, p. 28; Theorem 6.14, p. 60
sources.match: The cyclotomic t-structure is left complete, with genuinely cyclotomic truncations.

nodes.title: TR as V-complete topological Cartier modules
nodes.statement: For X∈CycSp_T,p let TR^{n+1}(X) be the iterated pullback of X^{hC_{p^n}}, …, X^{hC_p}, X over (X^{tC_p})^{hC_{p^{n−1}}}, …, X^{tC_p}, using can and Frobenius. The restriction tower defines TR(X). It has a natural topological Cartier structure and is right adjoint to M↦M/V. On bounded-below objects the counit TR(X)/V→X is an equivalence, TR is fully faithful and t-exact, and its essential image consists exactly of V-complete bounded-below topological Cartier modules. For bounded-below M, TR(M/V)≃lim_n M/V^n is its V-completion. On genuine bounded-below models, TR agrees with RT.2/tr-and-genuine-tc, including R,F,V.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Spectra, functor categories and all limits are coherent infinity-categorical objects.
proofSteps: Construct the TR norm factorization from the iterated pullback and its compatible projections (AN Construction 3.18). Prove the quotient adjunction by the mapping-fiber formula, Proposition 3.17.
Apply the Tate orbit lemma to the TR^n restriction fibers and commute Tate with their uniformly bounded-below limit. This proves the counit for bounded-below X (Lemma 3.19).

Identify TR(M/V) with lim_n M/V^n via the finite restriction fiber sequences; this gives completion and the essential image (Theorem 3.21, Proposition 3.22). Compare R,F,V with the genuine restriction pullbacks.
acceptance: TR(X)/V recovers X for bounded-below X with its cyclotomic structure, not merely its underlying spectrum.
The unbounded category is excluded from the essential-image and inverse-limit completion formulas.

sources.locator: Propositions 3.17 and Construction 3.18, pp. 24–25; Lemma 3.19, p. 25; Theorem 3.21 and Proposition 3.22, p. 26
sources.match: The quotient/TR adjunction becomes an equivalence onto V-complete objects in the bounded-below range.

nodes.title: The derived V-complete Cartier heart
nodes.statement: TR identifies the heart of CycSp_T,p with the full subcategory of derived V-complete p-typical Cartier modules. For every bounded-below X and every integer i, the Cartier module corresponding to π_i^cycX is (π_iTR(X),F,V). A bounded-below topological Cartier module is V-complete iff every π_i is derived V-complete. The heart equivalence is an equivalence of abelian categories; it is not an identification of the underlying spectra of a heart object and its Cartier module.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Spectra, functor categories and all limits are coherent infinity-categorical objects.
proofSteps: Use t-exactness and full faithfulness of TR to embed the heart into discrete topological Cartier modules, identified with Cart_p.

Apply the discrete completeness criterion and the essential-image theorem. For the degreewise completeness criterion, induct on finite Postnikov intervals and pass to the left-complete limit (AN Proposition 3.28).
Take π_i of the t-exact TR functor to obtain the Cartier realization of cyclotomic homotopy.
acceptance: For a perfect F_p-algebra k, the Cartier realization of THH(k) is W(k) with its F,V (AN Theorem 6.14); higher underlying homotopy of THH(k) remains visible after forgetting the heart embedding.

sources.locator: Theorem 3.26, p. 28; Proposition 3.28, pp. 28–29; discussion after Theorem 1, p. 3; Theorem 6.14, p. 60
sources.match: Derived V-complete Cartier modules are exactly the cyclotomic heart and their groups compute π_*TR.

nodes.title: TR detects cyclotomic quasi-isogenies
nodes.statement: For a map f:X→Y of bounded-below objects in CycSp_T,p, the following are equivalent: each π_i^cyc(f) is an isogeny in the heart; each bounded-above truncation τ_{≤n}^cyc(f) is an isogeny; and TR(f) is a quasi-isogeny of spectra. Isogeny denominators may depend on i or n. For a p-completed application, apply the statement in the p-complete setting with its preserved bounded-below hypotheses. TC_T,p followed by p-completion preserves these quasi-isogenies. Underlying spectral rational equivalence alone does not suffice.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Spectra, functor categories and all limits are coherent infinity-categorical objects.
proofSteps: Use the heart equivalence to identify π_i^cyc(f) with π_iTR(f) carrying F,V.
For each degree apply the Cartier approximate-inverse correction: multiplying g by its isogeny denominator makes both operator defects vanish. No uniform bound across all degrees is required.

Left-complete truncation and finite extension arguments identify the homotopy-object and Postnikov definitions. After p-completion TC_T,p(X) identifies with fib(1−F:TR(X)→TR(X)) by AN Remark 2.5. Fibers preserve degreewise isogenies: a bound in each of two adjacent degrees suffices. On bounded-below spectra derived p-completion preserves degreewise quasi-isogenies, by finite Postnikov windows. This proves the TC assertion without a false lower connectivity bound for uncompleted circle-equivariant TC.
acceptance: THH(F_p) has underlying spectrum quasi-isogenous to zero but is not quasi-isogenous to zero in the cyclotomic category: TC(F_p;ℤ_p) has π_0=π_−1=ℤ_p.
Degreewise denominators are permitted; a single annihilator for all homotopy groups is not required.

sources.locator: Definition 2.18 and following paragraph, p. 12; Proposition 3.1 and introductory paragraph of §3.1, p. 15
sources.match: TR detects quasi-isogenies through the Cartier heart, and TC with p-complete coefficients preserves them.
The fiber of 1−F on TR compares with circle-equivariant TC by a p-adic equivalence.

nodes.title: TR with a null cyclotomic Frobenius
nodes.statement: If X∈CycSp_T,p is bounded below and a T-equivariant nullhomotopy of its Frobenius X→X^{tC_p} is given, the TR pullback tower splits to give TR(X)≃∏_{n≥0}X_{hC_{p^n}}, where C_{p^0} is trivial. If the underlying X is quasi-isogenous to zero, then X is quasi-isogenous to zero in CycSp_T,p. The product uses homotopy orbits, not homotopy fixed points. Nullhomotopy after forgetting T is not the stated hypothesis.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Spectra, functor categories and all limits are coherent infinity-categorical objects.
proofSteps: The specified equivariant nullhomotopy splits the iterated TR pullbacks into the homotopy-orbit fibers of the norm sequences.

For a fixed homotopy degree j, bounded-below X permits a finite Postnikov range to compute π_j of every X_{hC_{p^n}}. The same annihilator for that range works for all n, since homotopy orbits preserve an annihilation map. This uniformity makes the product quasi-isogenous to zero.
Apply TR detection; do not infer the claim merely by commuting rationalization with an infinite product.
acceptance: A bounded-below spectrum with a single annihilation map has a uniform annihilator on all the product factors.
Without a null Frobenius THH(F_p) is the counterexample, so spectral p-torsion cannot replace the equivariant nullhomotopy.

sources.match: A null circle-equivariant Frobenius gives the homotopy-orbit product and the quasi-isogeny consequence.
The iterated pullback model fixes the product factors and structure maps.

nodes.title: Positively graded cyclotomic spectra
nodes.statement: A nonnegatively graded p-typical cyclotomic spectrum is a family of T-spectra (X_i)_{i≥0} with equivariant maps φ_i:X_i→(X_{pi})^{tC_p}. Morphisms and their homotopies intertwine these maps. The category is the coherent lax equalizer for the endofunctor (X_i)↦((X_{pi})^{tC_p}). Its underlying cyclotomic spectrum is ⊕_i X_i, using the canonical comparison from the sum of Tate terms to the Tate of the sum. Truncation X_{≤n} sets weights >n to zero and retains the induced Frobenius. For i>0, the fiber of X_{≤i}→X_{≤i−1} has null Frobenius because pi>i. The weight-zero fiber has no such conclusion.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Spectra, functor categories and all limits are coherent infinity-categorical objects.
proofSteps: Form Fun(ℕ_discrete,Sp) with graded tensor whose degree is the sum of input weights; encode the p-fold tensor-power diagonal by φ_i landing at weight pi.
Form the lax equalizer for its Frobenius endofunctor, then the underlying direct-sum functor with its canonical Tate comparison; equivalence of that comparison is unnecessary.
The truncation maps are compatible because p increases positive weights. On a single positive-weight fiber the target pi is absent, giving the nullhomotopy.
acceptance: A Frobenius preserving each positive weight is a different structure and gives the wrong graded THH reduction.

sources.locator: §3.1, pp. 15–16, paragraphs before Proposition 3.3; Appendix A, pp. 56–60
sources.match: Graded cyclotomic Frobenius multiplies the weight by p; truncations are cyclotomic.

api.name: GradedCyclotomicSpectrum
api.statement: A family with φ_i:X_i→(X_pi)^{tC_p} and coherent morphisms.

api.name: GradedCyclotomicSpectrum.toCyclotomic
api.statement: Sum the weights and assemble Frobenius via the canonical map into Tate of the sum.

api.name: GradedCyclotomicSpectrum.truncate
api.statement: Kill weights >n, producing a compatible inverse tower of cyclotomic objects.

api.name: GradedCyclotomicSpectrum.positive_fiber

tests.name: GradedCyclotomicSpectrum.weight_zero
tests.statement: An arbitrary cyclotomic X placed in degree zero retains its original Frobenius. In particular THH(F_p) at weight zero is not forced to be cyclotomically torsion.

tests.name: GradedCyclotomicSpectrum.positive_single

tests.name: GradedCyclotomicSpectrum.zero

tests.name: GradedCyclotomicSpectrum.square_zero_weights

nodes.title: Graded cyclotomic torsion and connective convergence
nodes.statement: Let X be a nonnegatively graded cyclotomic spectrum. Suppose X_0=0, the connectivity of X_i tends to infinity as i→∞, and ⊕_iX_i is quasi-isogenous to zero as a spectrum. Then ⊕_iX_i is quasi-isogenous to zero in CycSp_T,p. In this situation, for every j the maps π_jTR(X)→π_jTR(X_{≤n}) are isomorphisms for all sufficiently large n. More generally a tower of bounded-below cyclotomic objects with fibers of X→X_n becoming arbitrarily connective has this TR convergence. No assertion of strong convergence for arbitrary unbounded filtrations is included.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p. Spectra, functor categories and all limits are coherent infinity-categorical objects.
proofSteps: Use the increasing connectivity to identify X with the inverse limit of finite weight truncations. The error fibers become arbitrarily connective in the cyclotomic t-structure.
TR is t-exact on bounded-below objects and preserves limits as a right adjoint. Consequently π_jTR stabilizes in the finite truncations, using the same connectivity estimates.

Each positive-weight fiber is spectrally quasi-isogenous to zero and has null Frobenius. Apply the null-Frobenius theorem inductively to the finite tower; then stabilize in each degree and use TR detection.
acceptance: The zero weight hypothesis is essential: THH(F_p) placed in weight zero violates the conclusion.
The proof proves stabilization separately for each homotopy degree and never exchanges an arbitrary infinite product with rationalization.

sources.locator: Proposition 3.3 and its proof, p. 16; Proposition 3.5, pp. 16–17
sources.match: Positive graded truncations with increasing connectivity reduce quasi-isogenies to null-Frobenius fibers.
The right adjoint and its t-exactness provide the needed bounded-below limit control.

nodes.title: Polynomial extension of the graded trace
nodes.statement: For i≥0 and a quasisyntomic ring R, the graded map of TC(R;ℤ_p)→HC⁻(R;ℤ_p) factors naturally as ℤ_p(i)(R)→LΩ_R^{≥i}→Hodge-completed LΩ_R^{≥i}. Here LΩ is p-completed derived de Rham relative to ℤ_p before Hodge completion. Import polynomial left Kan extension of ℤ_p(i) from PR.4/syntomic-connectivity, using only its left Kan extension assertion; the construction owns the trace factorization, not a second syntomic complex. For p-torsion-free quasisyntomic R, the Hodge-completed right-hand map from the TC Beilinson square, after multiplying by p^{N(i)} with N(i) independent of R, refines to ℤ_p(i)(R/p)→p^{−N(i)}LΩ_R. Its rationalization is the χ_i used by RT.3b/graded-beilinson-square. The construction is an input to that square, not an import of its conclusion. On all p-complete animated rings the extension is defined by completed polynomial left Kan extension; completeness of the motivic filtration on every such input is not asserted.
hypotheses: Fix a prime p and i≥0. R is quasisyntomic; for χ_i require p-torsion-free R as in AMMN’s lowercase qSyn_Zp. Every completion is derived.
proofSteps: On quasiregular semiperfectoid covers, the two-degree Postnikov window of TC→HC⁻ gives the map into Hodge-completed LΩ^{≥i}. Descend using trace-flat-descent and the syntomic graded comparison.

On finite p-complete polynomial algebras the Hodge filtration is finite in each fixed polynomial dimension, so the uncompleted-to-Hodge-completed comparison identifies the targets. Restrict the trace and extend it using the imported syntomic polynomial left Kan property and DD.2’s definition of p-completed uncompleted de Rham.

The ordinary TC Beilinson square and its uniform quasi-isogeny bounds give an integral multiple of the completed χ_i before rationalization. Apply the same polynomial extension to the functor R↦ℤ_p(i)(R/p), obtaining χ_i with denominator depending only on i (AMMN proof of 6.17).

The PR.4 input is independently prismatic and does not depend on RT.3b. Its remaining algebraic proof audit remains at that supplier. Never use RT.6/ammn-filtered-interface, which consumes the graded square.
acceptance: Completion of the factored trace recovers the QRSP Postnikov-window map.
The denominator p^{N(i)} is independent of the ring; ring-dependent denominators do not give the natural isogeny statement.

sources.locator: Theorem 5.1(2), p. 25; Proposition 5.32, pp. 33–34; proof of 5.1(2) and Construction 5.33, pp. 34–35; Construction 6.16 and proof of Theorem 6.17, pp. 44–45
sources.match: Polynomial extension removes Hodge completion from the graded trace and from the integral multiple of χ_i.
